_meta.note: Industry snapshots — nested models of the forces acting on the AI pipeline. Curated editorial layer (the thesis in structured form); verify current state before citing. Each snapshot: what it is, why it moves the thesis, what to watch.

snapshots.title: The power wall
snapshots.summary: Data-center power demand is growing faster than grid interconnection, turbine supply, and transformer manufacturing can absorb. Electricity, not silicon, is becoming the binding constraint of the buildout.
snapshots.thesis_impact: Shifts chokepoint gravity downstream: whoever controls generation, interconnection queues, and grid equipment taxes every layer above. Supports BK_INFRA overweight independent of chip cycle.
drivers: Interconnection queues measured in years (PJM/ERCOT)
Transformer and turbine lead times at multi-year highs
Nuclear PPAs signed at premium $/MWh (CEG–MSFT archetype)
On-site generation (fuel cells, gas) as queue bypass

watch.item: Hyperscaler capex guidance splits (compute vs facilities/power)
watch.why: Reveals where the constraint actually binds

watch.item: GEV/ETN/SU.PA backlog and book-to-bill
watch.why: Grid equipment is the slowest-clearing bottleneck

watch.item: New nuclear/PPA announcements per quarter
watch.why: Premium baseload pricing = scarcity signal

snapshots.title: Memory becomes the second monopoly
snapshots.summary: HBM converts commodity DRAM into an allocated, negotiated, near-sold-out product. Capacity decisions two years out determine accelerator supply, and packaging (CoWoS-class) is the coupling constraint.
snapshots.thesis_impact: The memory tier graduates from cyclical to chokepoint-adjacent; HBM allocation share is a leading indicator for accelerator shipments and for who wins the next accelerator generation.
drivers: HBM output sold out ~a year ahead across the big three
HBM4 transition raises stacking/packaging complexity again
Advanced packaging capacity is the coupling constraint between logic and memory

watch.item: SK Hynix / Micron / Samsung HBM capacity and allocation statements
watch.why: Direct read on the binding constraint

watch.item: DRAM spot vs contract divergence
watch.why: Conventional memory squeeze funds/starves HBM expansion

watch.item: CoWoS-class capacity adds at TSMC and OSATs
watch.why: Packaging gates both logic and memory into product

snapshots.title: Circular financing — the bubble's plumbing
snapshots.summary: Chip vendors invest in labs; labs commit compute spend to clouds; clouds buy chips. Money loops through the graph (NVDA→OpenAI→Oracle/CoreWeave→NVDA) inflating everyone's bookings simultaneously.
snapshots.thesis_impact: The core sensemaking question: how much end demand is real vs recycled capital? Circularity is measurable as cycles in this graph — rising loop volume without matching application revenue is the bubble signature.
drivers: Vendor financing at unprecedented scale (NVDA→OpenAI class commitments)
RPO/backlog figures inflated by intra-loop contracts (ORCL archetype)
Private lab valuations priced off compute commitments, not revenue

watch.item: AI application-layer revenue vs aggregate capex, quarterly
watch.why: The only exit from the loop is end-user money

watch.item: Terms of vendor-financing deals (equity vs prepay vs backstop)
watch.why: Determines who eats losses if demand disappoints

watch.item: Neocloud debt loads and GPU-collateralized lending
watch.why: Leverage inside the loop amplifies unwind speed

snapshots.title: The silicon curtain
snapshots.summary: US/NL/JP export controls versus Chinese counter-controls on gallium, germanium, and rare earths split the industry into blocs. Policy, not economics, sets addressable markets for the equipment tier.
snapshots.thesis_impact: Repricing mechanism for the whole WFE tier: each rule change moves 10–25% of revenue exposure. Counter-controls hit optics, power electronics, and magnets — the BK_INFRA underbelly.
drivers: BIS rule cadence (2022/2023/2024 pattern suggests annual tightening)
China indigenization push (SMIC/Big Fund III) reducing long-run TAM
Rare-earth and Ga/Ge counter-controls touching Western supply

watch.item: China revenue share in AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/TEL/ASML prints
watch.why: Direct exposure readout each quarter

watch.item: New BIS/METI/MOFCOM actions (see export_controls.json)
watch.why: Each action re-draws the map

watch.why: Indigenization speed sets the long-run bear case for controls

snapshots.title: Advanced packaging — the quiet chokepoint
snapshots.summary: Chip-on-wafer-on-substrate class packaging (and its substrate/materials chain: ABF, mask blanks, dicing) is the least-substitutable, least-visible link between fabricated silicon and shippable accelerators.
snapshots.thesis_impact: Small-cap monopolies (Ajinomoto, Disco, Ibiden) carry outsized systemic weight — the original AlphaTopology insight. Capacity announcements here predict accelerator supply 2–3 quarters out.
drivers: CoWoS capacity repeatedly the stated shipment constraint
ABF film and substrate expansion measured in years
Panel-level packaging as the next transition risk/opportunity

watch.why: The best public proxy for the constraint

watch.item: Ibiden/Unimicron expansion timelines
watch.why: Substrate lead the accelerator ramp

snapshots.title: The researcher diaspora
snapshots.summary: Frontier capability concentrates in a few hundred researchers whose movements found companies and redirect billions. Lab departures are leading indicators of new nodes and of lab trajectory changes.
snapshots.thesis_impact: Talent flow is the second money flow: OpenAI alumni founded Anthropic, SSI, Thinking Machines. Compensation escalation (9-figure packages) is itself a capex line and a bubble signal.
drivers: Acqui-hire structures replacing acquisitions (Inflection/Scale archetypes)
Compensation arms race for frontier researchers
Safety-vs-scale disagreements as the recurring departure trigger

watch.item: Senior departures from top labs (tracked in people_seed)
watch.why: Predicts new entrants and lab strategy shifts

watch.item: New lab funding rounds within months of departures
watch.why: The diaspora pattern repeating

snapshots.title: Embodiment — the next demand layer
snapshots.summary: Humanoid and industrial robotics is where AI compute demand escapes the data center. Early, hype-heavy, but structurally the same graph: actuators, compute platforms, and training data as new chokepoints.
snapshots.thesis_impact: Optionality layer on the thesis: if embodiment works, a second demand curve for silicon/power begins; its supply chain (reducers, actuators, sensors — heavily Japanese) mirrors the semiconductor chokepoint pattern.
drivers: Humanoid pilots at automotive/logistics scale (Figure, Optimus)
Robot-foundation-model progress (sim-to-real transfer)
Actuator/harmonic-reducer supply concentration in Japan

watch.item: Deployment counts moving from pilots to fleet orders
watch.why: The hype/reality gate

watch.why: Industrial base rate for the sector

snapshots.title: Rates, liquidity, and the duration trade
snapshots.summary: AI infrastructure is a duration asset: decade-payback capex funded in public markets and private credit. The rate/liquidity environment sets both the discount rate on the dream and the financing cost of the buildout.
snapshots.thesis_impact: The macro overlay every stage shares: multiple compression hits long-duration names (labs, neoclouds) hardest; credit tightening threatens leveraged loop participants first.
drivers: Private credit's growing share of data-center financing
Hyperscaler shift from cash-funded to debt-funded capex
Index concentration making AI the market's macro factor

watch.why: Financing stress shows here before equity
